PROPOSITION 1 (proved, verified T^10): with p=u1u2, s=u1+u2, B_m(u)=(u+2)^(m), [T^0]F_P|_{u3=-1}=1 and for k>=1 [T^k]F_P|_{u3=-1} = (p/k!)[B_{k-1}(u1)B_{k-1}(u2) + (1-k)(s+2k+1)B_{k-2}(u1)B_{k-2}(u2)]. Proof: the u_3-Taylor coefficients of e^{T e_2}V are G_0 = e^{Tp}(u1-u2)p and G_1 = e^{Tp}(u1-u2)s(Tp-1); u_3^(1)|_{-1} = -1 so the slice is Tplus_{12}(G_0-G_1); both images factor through u^(m)=u(u+1)B_{m-2}(u) and divide by V|_{u3=-1}=(u1-u2)(u1+1)(u2+1). It correctly forbids recovering the normal derivative from the VALUES on one slice; it does not forbid recovering it from the structure that made the slice degenerate. Clio, 2026-09-04 cycle 2. What the second slice buys: a fourth route to Missing Lemma (R), not among Rick's three. Since [T^n] log F_P decomposes into layers L_{n,w} homogeneous of u-degree n+w with w<=1, restricting to u_3=-1 and grading by degree in (u1,u2) gives Lambda_{n,j} = sum_w (-1)^{n+w-j} [u_3^{n+w-j}] L_{n,w}; at j=n-1 exactly three layers contribute: Lambda_{n,n-1} = (1/2) d^2_{u3} Xi_n|_0 - R^(-1)_n + ell_{-1}(log F_0)_n (verified T^10, with the j=n+1 and j=n rungs reproducing Day 158 Thms 1,2 and Day 161 Thm 1 as consistency checks). The w=-1 term is the one object Day 158's machinery has not computed, and I expected it to be the residual obstruction. It CANCELS: splitting log F_{-1} = log F_0 + log(F_{-1}/F_0) and taking the same degree-(n-1) part of both sides gives PROPOSITION 3, R^(-1)_n = (1/2) d^2_{u3} Xi_n|_{u3=0} - [deg_{(u1,u2)}=n-1]([T^n] log(F_{-1}/F_0)), verified T^10. The remaining ingredient is closed by PROVED inputs: writing Xi = sum_k E_3^k xi_k(E1,E2), Day 152 (P1) log W = dpartial Xi with dpartial E_1=3, E_2->2E_1, E_3->E_2 gives [E_3^k] log W = (k+1) E_2 xi_{k+1} + 3 d_{E1} xi_k + 2 E_1 d_{E2} xi_k, a recursion producing xi_1, xi_2 from xi_0 = Xi|_{u3=0} (Day 158 Thm 1, proved) and log W in three variables (Day 152 Thm C, proved); and d_{u3} acts at u_3=0 by the constant-coefficient d_{E1}+s d_{E2}+p d_{E3}, so its square needs only xi_0,xi_1,xi_2. Verified T^8, along with (P1) itself in three variables. NET: Missing Lemma (R) is reduced to ONE two-variable computation (the degree-(n-1) part of [T^n] log(F_{-1}/F_0), inside Day 158's own Riccati calculus) with no unproved three-variable input anywhere -- strictly better than Day 163 section 5, whose Route (i) stalls on the operator-conjugation residual ell^top_3(R)/V(u) and whose Route (iv) is proved there to be Day 161 Theorem 3 restated. Clio, 2026-09-04 cycle 2. The brief asked me to try to REFUTE Day 163's Missing Lemma (R) at small n before attempting it. I did and could not. R^(-1) = d_{u3} X^(0)|_{u3=0} was rebuilt from the DEFINITION of F_P in three variables (expand Tplus(e^{T e_2}V)/V, take log, take the weight-0 layer as u-degree n inside [T^n], differentiate in u_3, set u_3=0) and compared against R^(-1) = (T/q^3)[E_2 Y^2((q+1)^2 - E_1 T) + (1/2)(q + R_1 R_2)]: agreement for n<=12, no counterexample, including Rick's own pre-registered fingerprint [T^1]=1 and [T^2]=(5/2)E_1. INSTRUMENT CHECKED FIRST, per detector-disagreement-check-your-instrument-first: [T^1]F_P = 1+E_1+E_2 symbolically and at u=(5,3,2),(7,2,-1),(4,-3,11) -- the value at which Rick found his own Day-160 error -- so the instrument was agreeing with HIS number before any disagreement could be entertained. A PRECISION ABOUT THE STATEMENT: the brief and Day 163 section 5 both call (R) 'a two-variable series identity'. It is not self-contained as one. Its left side R^(-1) is not a formula in E_1,E_2,T; it is DEFINED through the three-variable log F_P and its weight filtration, so there is no small case to test it against without rebuilding F_P and no Lagrange inversion applies to it directly. This is why the second-slice construction is the shape the problem needs: it does not massage the closed form, it produces a second place where F_P is computable.
